lessons: Costs decide on gold: round trip about 5.7-5.9 bp (about $0.80 per oz in IS, under the protocol model) = 0.13-0.51 R per intraday trade, 25% of an H1 ATR vs 8-13% for DAX and FX; only rules with cost under about 0.05 R per trade (wide stops, few trades, multi-day holds) survive. A random entry loses about 0.25 R per trade.

Horizons that died on costs: M5/M15 lead-lag, 1 h channels, H1/H4 RSI2 and Bollinger fades, intraday ORB (gross +0.1 to +0.2 R vs cost 0.13 to 0.51 R), all seasonality trades (1-2 bp per hour vs 5.7 bp), micro ML below about 12 bp moves.

What survived: slow breakouts with a trailing stop (Donchian 10 days on 4 h bars, PF 1.356 IS, 1.53 on 43 trades in 2026 per the bilan) and the multi-day Asian-range breakout (conditional on low costs). Both depend on a few big trend trades and on gold's drift (long side in VAL).
Gold continues after big moves (hourly and daily): fades lose even before costs; mean reversion has no pre-cost edge at the daily horizon.

The one-position-at-a-time rule can manufacture the pass: always run the every-signal diagnostic (Trend VAL 0.91, ORB IS 1.06, meanrev 0.95). Also check long vs short separately (drift) and a random-entry or shifted-level placebo; pivots equal random lines.
IS winners often fail VAL: rn100_break_fresh 1.379 to 0.836, Trend t 2.37 is best of 48 correlated configs (p about 0.1 after selection), pivbb rules t 3.26 best of 40 (Bonferroni p about 0.045).

Cross-market, untuned generic rules give no better results than gold (net PF 0.70-1.05 over 4 families x 6 markets); FX/DAX cost hurdle is 2-3x lower but there is no gross edge there either. Cross-asset information is worth 0.04-0.09 R per trade.

Practical caveats found: data holes on gold M1 (59 partial days), reopen spread at 18:00 NY about 3x normal, weekend closures; engine has no OCO (workarounds in place); non-gold markets are bid-only with fixed spread in round 1.

Frozen criteria per protocol: PF >= 1.20, t >= 2, 2/3 years positive, neighbours median >= 1.10, stress x1.5 PF >= 1.05 (round 1); round 2 uses PF >= 1.12, t >= 2.5, n >= 250, random-timing null at 97.5%. Total 321 gold-lab configurations in round 1 across 6 tracks (48 ORB, 50 trend, 38 meanrev, 84 pivots, 24 seasonality, 77 crossasset).

lessons: Costs set the horizon: FX all-in is about 1 bp (usdjpy 0.71 bp in the lab frame), US indices about 0.8 to 1.2 bp, DAX about 1.0 bp, bitcoin about 3.1 bp, ether about 7.8 bp (ether 6.5 bp spread, silver 5.4 bp spread); FX effects exist before costs (gross daily t 2.9 to 4.1) but measure only 1 to 2 bp per trade, so they die.

Micro-scale and short-horizon rules die on costs: best-tenth accuracy 51 to 56% against 51 to 75% needed; lead-lag at the 1% tail on us indices and gold/silver is 0.3 to 4 bp against 0.8 to 6.7 bp of cost; the DAX close-run is a 5-minute trade worth 0.38 bp net and flips with a one-minute shift of the exit.

What survived as an edge in sample and validation: slow breakout/trend on gold and crypto (4h Donchian, 24 h-hold H1 breakouts), opening-candle and noise-area momentum on us100 only, Nasdaq-to-bitcoin follow, gold Friday afternoon, an ML-filtered crypto breakout; each with a thin net edge and shrinking in 2022-2025 (btc +0.31 R to +0.04 R).

Many in-sample passes failed the single validation look: B5 month-end fix with S&P sign (+3.95 bp t 4.65 to +0.72 bp t 0.57), squeeze breakout on gold (PF 1.25 to 0.80), event premium (PF 1.6 to 0.9), DAX late momentum, month-end night, stress gate; calendar rules with n under 100 are particularly unreliable.
Long-only profits on rising markets are not edge: dip rules gave PF 1.48 yet sat at the 85th percentile of the random-entry null; always show long and short separately and run the random-entry null.

Currencies and silver did not carry the trend/breakout rules that work on gold and crypto: all four frozen transfers lose on the FX basket (PF 0.92-0.98), and silver loses everywhere except the legacy 4h Donchian reference (net PF 1.14, t 1.08).

Indicator-style pivot, Bollinger, RSI and candle-pattern conditions on gold added nothing: 139 configs, almost all PF below 1; the only survivors are outer pivots or yesterday-close bands, not pivot-specific (placebo lines earn the same).

Entry timing and quote artefacts matter: ether-to-bitcoin burst (PF 1.5) collapses with a 1 to 2 minute delay; Tokyo gotobi fails at one minute late; real FX fills and cost frames must be measured before trust.

Winning days or weeks cannot be bought with exit shaping, pyramiding or stake rules: they move risk from the number of red weeks to their size; zero-edge controls reproduce 4 to 22 points of 'winning weeks'.

lessons: Costs kill short-horizon edges: FX gross edges are 1-2 bp against about 1 bp all-in on majors; FX crosses at night had +1.78 bp gross against 3.34 bp all-in; 40 shares 1.9-2.5 bp gross against 12-15 bp; silver spread 5.4 bp; gold reopen drift and FX weekend fade had no gross edge at all.
Edges under about 2x their cost did not survive; round 6 would need costs 44 % lower to break even.
Nothing below 60 minutes survives (micro 2-171 min failed; the ETH-to-BTC 5-min rule was a quote-lag artifact; anything living in one minute is not an edge).

Frozen transfers rarely work outside the home market: 117 of 126 breadth pairs failed; only trend breakouts (donch4h, orb_asia) transferred, and only to bitcoin and ether, which are one cluster (6 of 9 qualifiers on BTC/ETH).
Crypto short-horizon momentum lost 65-80 % of its edge per trade between sample and validation; gold and us100 lost 20-40 %.
A strong in-sample t does not protect (sess_8_8_13 t 3.9 to PF 1.03; EV_PREM t 2.7 to PF 0.91; month-end basket t 4.27 to PF 0.81); after about 1,500 trials the best noise rule reaches t 3.35.
The random-entry null is decisive: long-only rules on drifting markets (indices, bitcoin) look good against it only because of drift; the same-year null removed 063 and 042.

Profits come from few trades and losses are plain stops: the best 5 % of trades carry 144 % of the R; cutting early, targets, partial exits, break-even, pyramiding, stakes by conviction, clock or weights all lowered or did not raise the gain per unit of swing.
Mean reversion failed at every intraday and daily scale (gold fades, pivots, dip buying, night FX crosses, hedged pairs z-score).
Slow trend (50-day breakouts) has no gross edge on 14 markets or 40 shares and pays 19-49 bp of swaps.
Closest misses were one-sided, one-year or one-cluster results (IDXRS t 2.15 with 2020 carrying it; options-expiry week t 1.65; Coinbase premium buy side t 2.38).
Many ideas close for lack of events: a single market needs at least 250 signals, which rules out rare-event ideas.
Breadth cannot reach the user's demand: the ten rules form about 3 independent clusters; adding all 9 qualifiers moved in-sample weekly Sharpe only 2.9 to 3.3.
